description.narrative: The Project consists of the development, financing, construction, operation, and maintenance of a 50 MWac solar PV plant at Selebi Phikwe in Botswana. The Project will be supplying power to Botswana Power Corporation (BPC) under a 25-year Power Purchase Agreement (PPA), signed on August 31, 2022. The Project was bid under a competitive process conducted by BPC in October 2020 and awarded to Scatec in August 2021.

The main expected project-level outcomes stem from increased access to reliable electricity through investment in renewable energy. Botswana is currently facing energy insecurity and loadshedding due to a demand deficit and dependencye on imports from South Africa. The project is expected to increase the installed generation capacity of Botswana by 11 percent at an affordable tariff and thereby contributing to reduced loadshedding and enhanced reliability. Currently Botswanas power generation is composed of coal fired power stations, diesel peakers and imports from South Africa, which is still mostly coal based. This project therefore also supports in the decarbonization of the regional power network. The anticipated market creation effects include improved competitiveness, deriving from support to the countrys first utility scale project-financed IPP project, with important demonstration effects. This investment also supports Botswanas efforts to increase resilience, by demonstrating a commercially viable and sustainable way to transition out of its current expensive and unreliable dependence on fossil fuel based energy and imports from South Africa.

name.narrative: The Project is located close to Selebi Phikwe town and will interconnect to the 220kV transmission line between Selebi Phikwe and Phokoje substation. The Phokoje substation is situated on Southern African Power Pool (SAPP) north-south 400kV transmission backbone providing the project a very stable point of interconnection as well as a strategic location in respect of the SAPP. The Project will cover an area of 121ha and will have an installed peak capacity of 60MW, making use of single axis trackers and bifacial solar panels.
